newsitem.title: FRANCE: Ranariddh warns of civil war in Cambodia.
newsitem.headline: Ranariddh warns of civil war in Cambodia.

text.p: Ousted Cambodian First Prime Minister Prince Norodom Ranariddh warned on Tuesday that a new civil war could sweep his homeland if his rival Hun Sen refused to negotiate Ranariddh's return to power.
"I am willing to see Hun Sen to solve this problem in an existing legal framework, but if we cannot, there would be, alas, a civil war in my poor country," Ranariddh told a news conference in Paris.

Ranariddh, toppled by Hun Sen, Cambodia's second prime minister who shared power with him in an ungainly two-headed coalition government, urged the international community not to recognise the new regime and said he was going to the United States on Wednesday to address the United Nations Security Council.
"I am asking the international community to take a clear position and to never recognise a government resulting from a coup d'etat," he told reporters.

Ranariddh had fled Cambodia for France last Friday, a day before the outbreak of the fighting between his troops and forces loyal to Hun Sen which led to his ouster. Hun Sen accused Ranariddh of teaming up with deserters from the deadly Khmer Rouge guerrilla group.
Ranariddh denied he was in contact with the guerrilla group but said that if they fought on his behalf in Cambodia, "there is nothing I can do about that".
